correctness.rationale: The terminal-edge arborescence/ordering bijection gives exact class multiplicities. Two heavy outgoing types would force at least three orderings, so the heavy-edge subgraph is functional. A directed-cut argument bounds off-cycle heavy edges by three and reduced cycle weights by eleven, proving completeness of the finite 12-bounded census. Its 316 independently listed canonical profiles yield 18 rational-series terms. A compiled complete word census through length 21 independently reproduces all coefficients; the coefficient checker agrees through length 120. A finite check alone is not used as an all-length proof.

value.rationale: Exactly-two classes are the first nontrivial reconstruction failures when all length-three substring multiplicities are observed. Their complete exact linear quasipolynomial law for all n, accompanied by the 316-profile structural classification, refines known singleton and total-class statistics and demonstrates a sharp gap between linear doubleton count and degree-six total class growth. The 2/3 periodic fluctuations are intrinsic to pumpable de Bruijn cycles, not an arbitrary finite slice.
